rules.title: Tenant Protection Act rent cap (AB 1482)
rules.requirement: Over any 12 months, rent can go up by at most 5% plus local inflation (CPI), and never more than 10%.

rules.exemptions: Housing built in the last 15 years; single-family homes and condos owned by individuals (with notice); units covered by stricter local rent control

rules.title: Statewide just-cause eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in the unit 12 months, the landlord may end the tenancy only for a reason listed in the law, stated in the written notice.
rules.exemptions: Newer buildings (15 years), owner-occupied duplexes, some single-family homes

rules.requirement: A landlord may not ask for a security deposit larger than one month's rent.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords (natural person owning max 2 properties, max 4 units) may ask for two months

rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: A screening fee may only cover the actual cost of the screening, up to a CPI-adjusted maximum, and no fee may be charged if no unit is available.
rules.quoted_span: to rent a residential property from an applicant, the landlord or their agent may charge, pursuant to subdivision (c), that applicant an application screening fee to cover the costs of obtaining information about the applicant.

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban (FEHA, SB 329)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse or screen out applicants because they pay with a housing voucher or other lawful source of income.

rules.title: Common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to coerce others to adopt its recommended prices.
rules.quoted_span: This bill would also make it unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce.

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance annual increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the yearly increase is limited to the amount set by the Rent Board: 1.6% from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: Certificate of occupancy on or before 1979-06-13
rules.exemptions: Newer buildings; single-family homes and condos (Costa-Hawkins)
rules.interaction: Stricter local rent control: the state cap (CA-RENT-01) yields to this rule.

rules.title: SF ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not sell or use algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span:
New law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.requirement: Rent increases in RSO buildings are limited to the yearly percentage set by the Los Angeles Housing Department.
rules.coverage_conditions: Built (certificate of occupancy) on or before 1978-10-01

rules.title: San Diego automated rent price-fixing ban
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use or sell algorithmic devices that set rents using nonpublic competitor data.
rules.quoted_span:
Complex, AI-driven price-fixing software is used across San Diego to suggest the highest rental pricing 
that a rental home can yield.

rules.title: Rent Security Deposit Act
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not be more than one and a half months' rent.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with 2 or fewer units (unless tenant opts in); seasonal rentals
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a home only for one of the good causes listed in the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with 2 or fewer units
rules.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act,  N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect 
blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in 
the State.
